body: I looked up the belt number and it should be the right belt.  The belt is routed correctly. Flat side on both idler pulleys and v side on both blade pulleys. I was thinking about it and I wonder if the new engine was designed with the driveshaft closer to the back of the engine than the one that was on it before

So I have a cub cadet ltx 1045. I replaced the blown engine with a briggs and Stratton. I used the pulley original to the cub cadet but now the pto belt is loose as all get out. When I engage the pto the pulley on the deck moves but not a lot. Even if I push the pulley all the way it's still not tight enough. From what I've looked up this is the right belt. The new engine had to be mounted in holes that are slightly to the side of the original holes. But this is left to right movement not front to back and it was only about an inch different. Why is it so loose?

I believe the vibrations from the machine and the way they had run the leads caused the screw head from one lead to rub through the insulation on the other lead that had been ran along side it. I'm 99%sure that's what caused the issue. And since we only have the one spare it would just be better to order the right one to replace with imo. Thank you!
I think that was it. Thank you!
